transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-24 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Liam Soto (Redwood CSM), Marcus Lee (BluePeak Head of ML), Sabrina Ortiz (BluePeak VP Product), Elliot Ng (BluePeak Platform)
Recording: https://app.fireflies.example/recordings/bpa-2026-03-24-9f7a2c (internal reference)

Summary: quick mid-quarter health check focused on usage spikes, cost drivers, one reliability incident in March, and roadmap alignment for a proposed Dedicated pilot to improve unit economics. Agreed next steps include sharing a cost projection, running a focused perf benchmark on larger context lengths, and sharing SOC2 + SSO artifacts.

Topics covered: usage trends, token distribution, p95/p99 latency, cost-per-infer, KV cache opportunities, Dedicated pilot sizing, canary rollout plan for model v2.1, security artifacts (SOC2/ISO), SAML SSO, A/B evaluation for quality.

Action items (brief): see metadata action_items for owners/due dates.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: okay, good afternoon everyone, thanks for jumping on, we've got about an hour, we'll run through usage and cost, then Priya will talk perf and reliability and then Liam will recap ops and next steps. Marcus, Sabrina, Elliot you good?
[00:12] Marcus: yeah all good, thanks. sorry I'm a bit late - pulled from a stand.
[00:20] Sabrina: all good here.
[00:22] Jordan: quick note, recording on. if anything super sensitive we'll flag and stop.
[00:30] Priya: cool, I'll start with the top-line: we pulled the last 90 days of telemetry from your account (crm id CRM-2026-0287-BPA) — token consumption's up ~33% month-over-month, largely driven by longer-context chat use in your support automation flow. the 95th percentile seq length moved from ~1.8k to ~4.6k.
[00:47] Elliot: yep that's accurate, the new triage agent pulls full conversation context now, so the average context increased.
[00:55] Marcus: part of that was intentional; quality improved, but cost got us a little surprised. what are the levers here?
[01:05] Priya: right — main levers: prefix/K-V cache (we sometimes see it transcribed as K-V cash in the logs), smarter batching, quantization profiles, and routing to a dedicated pool for hot routes. caching looks like low-hanging fruit — your repeat prefixes account for ~22% of tokens. enabling prefix cache on the support route could shave ~12–18% immediately.
[01:29] Marcus: 12–18% is great. does that affect tail latency?
[01:35] Priya: small effect on median, but helps p95 because we cut token regens; also reduces load, so headroom improves. we measured p99 improvements in a similar customer after enabling warm KV cache.
[01:48] Sabrina: curious about the Dedicated option — price vs hosted, and how quickly it pays for itself.
[01:55] Jordan: good question — we ran an initial projection: with your current baseline spend (~$18k/mo) and projected growth to $24k/mo in two months, a 6-month Dedicated pilot with a modest reserved pool plus burst capacity looks like it could be 15–28% cheaper per effective token once you hit steady throughput. we'll send the tailored pricing sheet.
[02:18] Marcus: want to see the math, please. also we need to understand what happens during incidents — we had that outage last Wed where several requests error'd out.
[02:28] Priya: on the outage: quick recap — 2026-03-18 at 03:12 UTC we saw a model fallback cascade on the support route when the preferred instance type hit a transient GPU OOM during a large batch job. traffic spiked, fallback routing introduced higher latency, and a misconfigured retry logic caused a small window of 500s. we have the traces attached in the shared folder; Elliott, do you have the incident timeline from your side?
[02:56] Elliot: yes, we saw p99 go from ~920ms to ~3.6s for about 12 minutes. our infra autoscaler responded but the retry storm made it worse initially.
[03:09] Priya: we've proposed a change: limit retry fanout, enable instantaneous fallback to a smaller-architectural-var model (we call them compatible variants) and enable earlier autoscale thresholds. also, set a fast path for essential endpoints so they don't queue behind heavy batch jobs.
[03:28] Marcus: sounds good. is that something Redwood can push or do we change it on our side?
[03:34] Priya: it's a joint change — Redwood will update the routing policy and provide a recommended autoscale rule; BluePeak will validate in staging and sign off.
[03:42] Jordan: Liam will own the rollout and CTA. Liam?
[03:46] Liam: yup, I'll coordinate a canary rollout plan: canary 5% traffic for 24h, monitor latency and error budget, then 25% for 12h, then full. we'll produce a rollback playbook.
[03:59] Sabrina: perfect. what about quality regressions? we've been sensitive to drift since last model swap.
[04:06] Priya: we'll hook your regression eval suite into Redwood's monitoring — you already have two core prompts flagged; add two more edge prompts and we'll trigger alerts if quality drops by >4% in eval scores. Liam will set up the alert.
[04:22] Marcus: on the Dedicated pilot sizing — what GPU types do you recommend? A100? H100?
[04:29] Priya: for your mix (mostly medium-length chat with occasional long context summaries) H100 in mixed-precision quantized mode gives the best throughput per dollar; A100 is a lower-cost-per-hour option if you prefer. we'll include both scenarios in the cost sheet. also quantization profiles — 4-bit vs 8-bit — affect output quality slightly; we'll recommend a conservative 8-bit profile for customer-facing flows initially.
[04:55] Elliot: any quick wins we can do before a pilot to lower cost?
[04:58] Priya: yes: enable prefix cache, reduce prompt verbosity where possible, add a short-term TTL on some conversational metadata, and tune batching windows for the support route from 50ms to 80ms — small latency trade for better throughput. should shave another ~8–12%.
[05:17] Jordan: on the governance/security side — Sabrina had questions last time about SOC 2 artifacts and SSO. Jordan, can you speak to that?
[05:25] Jordan: sure. Redwood is SOC 2 Type II certified; we maintain a standard artifact bundle. we'll share a subset that you can use for your security review (NDA-permitted). on SSO we support SAML and OIDC; we'll provide the SAML playbook and a quick-run checklist for your identity team.
[05:40] Sabrina: do you support SCIM for provisioning?
[05:43] Jordan: yes, we do. we'll include docs for SAML + SCIM.
[05:47] Marcus: data residency question — can Dedicated be deployed in our GCP project or via VPC peering?
[05:53] Priya: Dedicated can be VPC-connected or private where we deploy an appliance into your VPC (private deployment). for strict residency you can use Redwood Private on-prem or in your GCP region. we'll map options in the proposal.
[06:06] Sabrina: excellent. can you also confirm logging retention for audit purposes? we need 1 year.
[06:12] Jordan: we can provide 12 months of audit logs as an add-on; include that in the quote.
[06:18] Marcus: back to costs — curious about potential savings from moving long-tail inference to a cheaper variant or offloading embeddings.
[06:26] Priya: two patterns: route expensive summarization jobs to a cheaper quantized summarization model, or precompute embeddings in batch for less critical background tasks. both reduce on-demand token cost.
[06:38] Marcus: ok let's show us the numerics.
[06:41] Priya: we'll show three scenarios in the spreadsheet: hosted baseline, hosted + caching/batching changes, and dedicated pilot with reserve+burst.
[06:49] Jordan: quick question for product: Sabrina, what's your timeline for roadmap decisions?
[06:54] Sabrina: if the Dedicated pilot demonstrates ~20% cost savings and no regressions, we want to decide by end of Q2 (June 2026). internal procurement windows are mid-July for budget cycle.
[07:06] Jordan: good, so pilot in April/May fits.
[07:10] Marcus: any blockers on our side? Elliot is there anything else we need to pull?
[07:14] Elliot: I'll pull token distribution and p99 latency slices and the incident logs and drop them in the shared folder by Friday (2026-03-27).
[07:22] Jordan: perfect. Priya, quick on perf benchmark plan — what do you need from BluePeak?
[07:27] Priya: table of representative prompts, the top 10 heavy routes, and a staging endpoint with a recent snapshot of traffic. also access to your eval set we mentioned.
[07:36] Marcus: we'll prepare that.
[07:38] Sabrina: one more Q on billing granularity — can you show per-route token billing?
[07:42] Jordan: yes, Redwood Console surfaces token-level breakdowns per route and model; we'll send a screenshot and a short video walkthrough.
[07:51] Marcus: nice.
[07:52] [08:00] Priya: small note — sometimes our auto-transcripts render model names wrong, e.g., Redwood Optimize gets transcribed as Redwood Opti-mize, or dedicated as Dedicate, so just FYI when searching.
[08:13] Jordan: ha good to know.
[08:15] Liam: I'll own the canary runbook and the quality regression alert setup. I'll also schedule the perf session with Priya for the week of 2026-04-05.
[08:25] Marcus: who will sign the pilot SOW?
[08:28] Jordan: we'll have a short SOW for the 6-week pilot — Jordan will share a draft, then legal review.
[08:34] Sabrina: timeline sounds good.
[08:36] Elliot: ok I'll upload logs.
[08:38] Jordan: any other blockers or questions?
[08:40] Marcus: none from me.
[08:41] Sabrina: no.
[08:42] Jordan: recap of next steps: Jordan sends pilot quote & SOW draft by 2026-03-26; Priya shares the cost projection scenarios and perf test plan by 2026-03-29; Elliot uploads telemetry by 2026-03-27; Liam schedules canary/runbook and the perf session for the week of 2026-04-05. Redwood to share SOC2 subset and SAML/SCIM docs by 2026-03-31.
[08:59] Marcus: thanks everyone.
[09:01] Jordan: thanks, we'll follow up in thread and close the loop on artifacts. meeting adjourned.
